prompt: A friend texts you late at night saying they had a terrible day and sent a crying emoji. Your first reaction is——

options.text: Call them on voice chat right away and try to make them laugh first
Listen to them quietly, speak lightly, but worry deeply about how much they're hurting
Ask what happened and help them sort things out piece by piece
Judge whether this deserves such distress, then decide if it's worth addressing

prompt: When a gathering just starts and no one's quite comfortable yet, the vibe is a bit awkward. You usually——

options.text: Find a concrete topic like food, drinks, or plans to steadily carry the conversation
Don't rush to fit in; just talk with people you actually click with
Observe others' states first, then slowly join in when the timing feels right
Proactively start conversations and heat up the room, even if it gets a bit loud

prompt: You've been misunderstood and the other person has already told others. You're more likely to——

options.text: Explain immediately to clear things up and avoid prolonging the awkwardness
Say 'never mind' on the surface, but replay it over and over in your head
Organize the backstory clearly and explain only the key facts
Not a big deal to explain; people who misunderstand you weren't that important anyway

prompt: When making an important decision, what do you rely on most——

options.text: A powerful emotional signal from deep within that you can't quite explain
The current atmosphere and mood; if it feels right, you'll move forward
Your intuitive judgment about people and situations, especially who's trustworthy
Rules, logic, risks, and success rates

prompt: When you like someone, what's your most typical state——

options.text: You naturally gravitate to talking with them, finding small ways to create presence
Your surface doesn't change much, but you amplify your feelings internally
You silently remember what they need and care for them through actions
You treat them distinctly different from others and don't hide your favoritism

prompt: Your most comfortable work state is——

options.text: You set your own pace and make your own calls; you don't like others interfering
When your mood is right your efficiency is high; when it's off, it crashes completely
You can work while talking, unbothered by a lively environment around you
Clear processes, standards, and right answers; the clearer the better

prompt: If you're responsible for onboarding a new person, you'd be the kind of mentor who——

options.text: Keeps encouraging them and telling them not to stress
Perceives their anxiety well but doesn't necessarily name it
Teaches them steps and reasoning carefully, hoping they get up to speed quickly
Assesses their potential first, then decides how much time to invest

prompt: When you're under a lot of stress, you're more like——

options.text: You start making lists and finding solutions, putting things back in order
Still trying to keep things light, not wanting others to worry
You get colder, don't want to explain, and prefer not to be bothered
You say it's fine, but alone you spiral thinking about it more and more

prompt: When someone cries hard in front of you, you'd most likely——

options.text: Hand them tissues and water, and try to lighten the mood
Sit beside them, don't rush them, and don't push advice
Once they're more stable, help them sort through what to do
Feel a bit impatient; you think prolonged emotional venting doesn't help

prompt: Which statement sounds most like your way of handling things——

options.text: Whether I like it and whether it's worth it—I know in my heart
Get the vibe right first, the rest will work itself out
So much of what I feel doesn't actually get said
If something can be explained clearly, don't rely on guessing

prompt: If someone says you're 'hard to understand,' it's probably because——

options.text: You're enthusiastic but sometimes suddenly too noisy
You seem understated, but your emotions have actually flipped many times inside
You're very logic-focused, like you're solving a problem rather than offering comfort
You're just cold to people who don't matter, sometimes even a bit mean

prompt: You're most easily moved by someone who——

options.text: Is sincere, stable, reliable, and makes you feel secure
Is clearly strong but willing to be your favorite person and let you treat them specially
Can match your enthusiasm and join you in the fun
Can see your unspoken emotions but doesn't force you to express them

prompt: After moving to a new neighborhood with lots of new shops and restaurants, you're more likely to——

options.text: Suddenly feel like visiting somewhere based on a mood, and if you like it you'll remember it forever
First check if it's convenient for kids, friends, or people you're close with
Not rush; slowly check things out and try places that appeal to you
Quickly get familiar with the area, knowing which places are best and most reliable

prompt: When someone suddenly disrupts your carefully made plans, you usually——

options.text: Feel a bit unhappy, but quietly adapt to the change
Point out the problem directly and demand a more logical approach
Act unaffected, but your emotions actually spiral immediately
Make sure everyone else is fine first, then deal with your own frustration

prompt: Facing new software, equipment, or rules you're unfamiliar with, you're more like——

options.text: You study the rules thoroughly first, then pick it up efficiently
If it doesn't feel right you'll put it aside and follow your own pace
Worry that others won't know how to use it, so you help everyone figure it out
You're a bit slow, not because you can't, just because you don't like being rushed

prompt: If you care deeply about someone, you're more likely to——

options.text: Be reserved with others, gradually showing your dependence only with them
Not say soft things, but stand firmly by their side
Your feelings grow deeper and deeper, so deep you can't easily step away
Can't help but take care of them, worrying if they've eaten well, slept well, been treated well

prompt: In a group, the role you typically play is——

options.text: The one who notices who's tired, who's falling behind, who needs care
Not necessarily the most outgoing, but you have your own rhythm and boundaries
The one who decides, pushes things forward, gets things moving
Quiet but deeply observant and emotionally aware

prompt: If someone is being treated unfairly, your reaction would be——

options.text: Calmly observe first; you won't immediately stand up
Speak back directly, even if the other person is stronger
You'll remember that unfairness deeply and feel hurt for them for a long time
Protect the person first, then handle everything else later

prompt: Which living environment makes you most comfortable——

options.text: Enough private space to hold deep feelings and creative inspiration
A slower pace, with flowers, light, and your own familiar little world
Safe, warm, with people coming and going, but everyone is well cared for
Everything efficient and orderly, knowing exactly where things are and how to do them

prompt: People most easily misunderstand you in this way——

options.text: They think you're lazy, but you're just slow-paced and slow to warm up
They think you're too domineering, but you just hate chaos and unfairness
They think you're cold, but you just don't share your emotions with many people
They think you're easygoing, but you're actually very serious about protecting others

prompt: You tend to express affection by——

options.text: Using 'I've got your back' rather than sweet words
Turning affection into daily care, visible in small thoughtful acts
Quietly drawing closer, occasionally acting a bit clingy, but only with special people
Your love grows heavier and heavier, until you can't control it

prompt: If a little kid suddenly throws a tantrum at home, you'd most likely——

options.text: Crouch down and sit with them, slowly letting them calm down
Explain the rules clearly so they understand what's allowed and what's not
Get struck by their emotions immediately, composed on the surface but troubled inside
Naturally pick them up, soothe them, rock them to sleep, and clean up the mess

prompt: What bothers you most at work——

options.text: Valuing only efficiency without considering people's condition and capacity
No feeling, no aesthetics, no space for emotion
Being constantly rushed, disrupted, with no rhythm of your own
There's clearly a better way, but no one's willing to implement it

prompt: Which statement sounds most like you——

options.text: Taking it slow is fine; living at your own pace is what matters
Say what needs saying, push back when necessary
The deepest love is often hidden in silence
Anyone I let into my heart, I'll seriously try to protect
